summary: Well-executed, artifact-backed paired study that measured the marginal verifier+single-repair effect on identical LLM-generated network-configuration candidates under explicit shared_initial_candidate semantics. Execution produced 250 intent pairs (500 episodes) with gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator; baseline pass = 249/250, guarded pass = 250/250, paired difference = +0.4 pp (95% CI [0.0,1.2 pp]), exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The run preserved rich execution artifacts and reconciled provider-call accounting. Major concerns are (1) an inconsistency between the preregistered top-level research question/hypothesis about sim→real (emulation vs production-like) and the actual confirmatory execution (synthetic/emulation partition only comparing baseline vs guarded), and (2) incomplete IEEE-formatted References in the manuscript bundle. These issues require explicit, archived clarifications or corrections before finalisation; otherwise the experimental execution, analysis, and archival practice are sound and reproducible.
critical_issues: Preregistration vs executed estimand mismatch: The preregistration text and H1 frame the primary confirmatory hypothesis as a sim-to-real (emulation vs production-like) paired comparison, but the executed confirmatory run and reported primary estimand are a within-partition paired comparison (baseline vs guarded) on the synthetic/emulation partition only. The manuscript and execution manifest do not explicitly mark the preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory hypothesis as unexecuted; the run incorrectly reports 'deviations_from_preregistration: []'. This is a mandatory disclosure/deviation that must be corrected.

References formatting and citation integrity: The manuscript text uses IEEE-style bracket markers (e.g., [1]–[6]) but the supplied manuscript evidence bundle does not contain a conventional IEEE-numbered References section with full bibliographic entries mapping to in-text markers. The submission must supply an ordinary IEEE bibliography (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/arXiv) that verifies each cited claim.

Preregistered confirmatory scope and claims need explicit narrowing: Several places (preregistration header, research-question framing) imply a sim-to-real confirmatory test; the paper must not imply that the preregistration’s sim-to-real confirmatory inference was performed unless the authors explicitly document that it was not executed and re-state the actual confirmatory estimand that was executed (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on synthetic/emulation partition).
required_revisions: Explicitly correct and disclose the preregistration/execution mismatch: In Methods and Preregistration sections (and in the Disclosure Statement if relevant), add a clear, prominent statement that the preregistered sim-to-real (emulation vs production-like) confirmatory hypothesis (H1) was not executed in this run, and that the executed confirmatory estimand was the paired difference (guarded − baseline) evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Update any sentence that could be read to claim the sim→real comparison was performed; do not present unexecuted preregistered inferential claims as completed results.

Replace the current cited_record_ids placeholder with a conventional IEEE-formatted References section (numbered entries) that maps each in-text bracketed citation to a full bibliographic entry. Ensure every citation used to support a claim actually contains and supports that claim; use the archived/verifiable evidence records to construct these entries.

Amend the manuscript's preregistration/deviations reporting: set 'deviations_from_preregistration' to list the above execution/estimand divergence, and include a short justification why confirmatory execution was limited to the synthetic/emulation partition (deterministic contract or other reason) and reference the archival manifest entries that document the executed contract.

Clarify provider-call accounting semantics in Methods: keep the current reconciliation text but add a single clear sentence stating that shared_initial_candidate means one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and reused for both condition episodes, and that provider_call_audit.condition_counts/stage_counts label instrumented stage counts rather than independent per-condition first-pass generation counts. Link these statements to the archived manifest paths/hashes already present.

Ensure that all in-text claims about preregistration, planned hypotheses, and confirmatory scope match the documented archived artifacts (preregistration SHA and execution manifest). If any language in Abstract, Introduction, Contributions, or Conclusion implies that the preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory test was performed, revise to avoid the implication.
optional_revisions: In Results or Discussion, add an explicit short paragraph quantifying the consequence of the observed baseline pass rate on statistical power (e.g., observed detectable effect vs original target) and note implications for future partition-specific confirmatory runs.
Report the exact binomial (Clopper–Pearson) confidence interval for the single repair-conversion rate (1/250) in addition to the paired bootstrap CI, to help readers interpret rare-event uncertainty.

If available in the archived artifacts, include a brief appendix-like table mapping in-text citation numbers to the archived evidence-record identifiers (OpenAlex/DOI/arXiv) to facilitate reviewer verification (this mapping can be kept concise and is acceptable because archives already preserve full provenance).
